capital.zh: 龙城（鄂尔浑河谷，具体位置不详）

summary.en: The first great steppe empire, forged by Modu Chanyu, the Xiongnu extracted tribute from Han China until Han offensives and internal splits divided them; the Northern Xiongnu were broken in 89–91 CE.
summary.zh: 冒顿单于缔造的匈奴是第一个强大的草原帝国，曾向汉朝索取岁贡，后因汉朝的反击和内部分裂而分化；北匈奴于公元89—91年被击溃。

sources.title: Sima Qian, Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian), ch. 110: the Xiongnu
Nicola Di Cosmo, Ancient China and Its Enemies (2002)
Thomas J. Barfield, The Perilous Frontier: Nomadic Empires and China (1989)
Wikidata Q188836

note: Wikidata gives century-level dates (3rd c. BCE–5th c. CE); 209 BCE–91 CE marks Modu’s accession to the Northern Xiongnu collapse. The Southern Xiongnu survived under Han until 216.

capital.zh: 吐火罗斯坦（都城不详，或在昆都士附近）

summary.en: The Hephthalites, often called White Huns, ruled from Bactria over Sogdiana, the Tarim and north-west India, defeated and killed the Sasanian king Peroz in 484, and were destroyed by the Turks and Sasanians around 560.
summary.zh: 嚈哒常被称为“白匈奴”，以巴克特里亚为中心统治粟特、塔里木和印度西北部，484年击杀萨珊国王卑路斯，约560年被突厥与萨珊联军所灭。

sources.title: Étienne de la Vaissière, “Is there a ‘nationality of the Hephthalites’?”, Bulletin of the Asia Institute 17 (2003)
Denis Sinor (ed.), The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990)
History of Civilizations of Central Asia, vol. III (UNESCO)
Wikidata Q26576

note: Wikidata gives 408–670 (including successor principalities); 450–560 is the conventional span of the imperial period. Individual rulers are poorly attested and omitted.

name.zh: 突厥汗国（第一突厥汗国）

summary.en: Founded by the Ashina clan, the Turkic Khaganate controlled the steppe from Manchuria to the Black Sea and the Silk Road trade, dealing with Sui-Tang China, Persia and Byzantium, before splitting into eastern and western khaganates.
summary.zh: 阿史那氏建立的突厥汗国控制着从东北亚到黑海的草原及丝绸之路贸易，与隋唐、波斯和拜占庭往来，后分裂为东、西两个汗国。

sources.title: Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Denis Sinor (ed.), The Cambridge History of Early Inner Asia (1990)
Wikidata Q15146034

note: Wikidata gives 551 as inception; 552 is the year of the victory over the Rouran in Chinese sources.

summary.en: Ilterish (Kutlug) revived Turkic independence from Tang rule in 682; under Bilge Qaghan, Kül Tegin and the adviser Tonyukuk the khaganate flourished, recording its history on the Orkhon steles before the Uyghurs overthrew it.
summary.zh: 682年骨咄禄（颉跌利施可汗）摆脱唐朝统治、复兴突厥；在毗伽可汗、阙特勤和谋臣暾欲谷时期汗国兴盛，并以鄂尔浑碑铭记述其历史，后被回鹘推翻。

sources.title: Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Talat Tekin, A Grammar of Orkhon Turkic (1968)
Wikidata Q4833446

summary.en: Successors of the Turks on the Mongolian plateau, the Uyghurs helped the Tang suppress the An Lushan rebellion, grew rich on the horse–silk trade, adopted Manichaeism and built the walled capital Ordu-Baliq before the Kyrgyz destroyed them.
summary.zh: 回鹘继突厥之后称雄蒙古高原，曾助唐平定安史之乱，借绢马贸易致富，奉摩尼教为国教，并修筑都城斡耳朵八里，后为黠戛斯所灭。

sources.title: Colin Mackerras, The Uighur Empire according to the T’ang Dynastic Histories (1972)
Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Wikidata Q831218

summary.en: A Persian dynasty ruling Transoxiana and Khurasan under nominal Abbasid suzerainty, the Samanids presided over a golden age of New Persian literature (Rudaki) and science, and converted Turkic neighbours to Islam.
summary.zh: 萨曼王朝是名义上臣属阿拔斯哈里发、统治河中与呼罗珊的波斯王朝，主持了新波斯语文学（鲁达基）和科学的黄金时代，并使邻近的突厥人皈依伊斯兰教。

sources.title: S. Frederick Starr, Lost Enlightenment: Central Asia’s Golden Age from the Arab Conquest to Tamerlane (2013)
Richard N. Frye, Bukhara: The Medieval Achievement (1965)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Sāmānid dynasty
Wikidata Q12150341

capital.zh: 八剌沙衮；喀什噶尔；撒马尔罕

summary.en: The first Turkic dynasty to adopt Islam, the Karakhanids took Bukhara from the Samanids in 999, later split into eastern and western khanates, and produced the earliest Islamic Turkic literature, such as the Kutadgu Bilig.
summary.zh: 喀喇汗国是第一个皈依伊斯兰教的突厥王朝，999年从萨曼王朝手中夺取布哈拉，后分裂为东西两部，并产生了《福乐智慧》等最早的伊斯兰突厥语文学。

name.zh: 纳斯尔·伊本·阿里（伊利克）

sources.title: Peter B. Golden, An Introduction to the History of the Turkic Peoples (1992)
Yusuf Khass Hajib, Kutadgu Bilig (Wisdom of Royal Glory), tr. Robert Dankoff (1983)
Wikidata Q494354

summary.en: Founded by the Liao prince Yelü Dashi after the Jurchen conquest of north China, the Qara Khitai ruled Central Asia as a Chinese-style, religiously tolerant empire until the Naiman Kuchlug usurped it and the Mongols destroyed it.
summary.zh: 辽朝宗室耶律大石在女真灭辽后西迁建立西辽，以汉式制度和宗教宽容统治中亚，后被乃蛮王子屈出律篡夺，最终为蒙古所灭。

sources.title: Michal Biran, The Empire of the Qara Khitai in Eurasian History (2005)
Liaoshi (History of Liao), ch. 30
Wikidata Q862304

capital.zh: 玉龙杰赤（库尼亚—乌尔根奇）；撒马尔罕（1212年起）

summary.en: Khwarazm-shahs of Turkic origin rose from Seljuk governors to rulers of an empire stretching from the Syr Darya to Iran; Muhammad II’s provocation of Genghis Khan brought its sudden destruction in 1219–1221.
summary.zh: 突厥裔的花剌子模沙从塞尔柱总督起家，建立起从锡尔河延伸到伊朗的帝国；摩诃末二世激怒成吉思汗，导致帝国于1219—1221年骤然覆灭。

sources.title: Ata-Malik Juvaini, Tarikh-i Jahangushay (The History of the World-Conqueror), tr. J. A. Boyle (1958)
C. E. Bosworth, “Khwarazmshahs”, Encyclopaedia Iranica
Wikidata Q63134381

summary.en: Created by Genghis Khan, the Mongol Empire became the largest contiguous land empire in history, linking China, Iran and Russia; after 1260 it divided into the Yuan, Ilkhanate, Golden Horde and Chagatai khanates under nominal Yuan supremacy.
summary.zh: 成吉思汗创建的蒙古帝国成为历史上疆域最大的连续陆地帝国，将中国、伊朗与罗斯连为一体；1260年后分裂为元朝、伊儿汗国、金帐汗国和察合台汗国，元朝皇帝名义上为共主。

sources.title: The Secret History of the Mongols, tr. Igor de Rachewiltz (2004)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Thomas T. Allsen, Mongol Imperialism (1987)
Wikidata Q12557

note: The end date 1368 follows Wikidata (fall of the Yuan); the unified empire effectively ended with the succession war of 1260–1264.

story.en:
The Great Mongol State proclaimed in 1206 conquered more land than any empire before it. Genghis Khan took north China’s Jin borderlands and Khwarazm; his son Ögedei finished the Jin, built Karakorum and sent armies into Rus’, Poland and Hungary; his grandsons Möngke, Hulagu and Kublai added Iran, Iraq, Yunnan and finally Song China.

It held together through a mobile court, the decimal army, the yam relay post with its stations and passes, and a census and tax system that drew on Uyghur, Khitan, Chinese and Persian administrators. Merchants and missionaries travelled under its protection, from William of Rubruck at Karakorum to Marco Polo in China.

After Möngke died in 1259 the succession war between Kublai and Ariq Böke split it into four khanates: the Yuan in China, the Ilkhanate in Iran, the Chagatai khanate in Central Asia and the Golden Horde on the western steppe. The last Yuan emperor fled Dadu in 1368, but Chinggisid descent remained the test of legitimacy on the steppe for centuries.
story.zh:
1206年建立的大蒙古国征服的土地超过以往任何帝国。成吉思汗夺取金朝北部边地和花剌子模；其子窝阔台灭金，建哈拉和林，并派大军进入罗斯、波兰和匈牙利；其孙蒙哥、旭烈兀和忽必烈又取得伊朗、伊拉克、云南，最终征服南宋。

维系这个帝国的是流动的宫廷、十进制军队、设有驿站和牌符的站赤（驿传）制度，以及任用畏兀儿、契丹、汉人和波斯官员的户口与赋税体系。商人和传教士在其保护下往来，从哈拉和林的鲁布鲁克到中国的马可·波罗。

1259年蒙哥去世后，忽必烈与阿里不哥的汗位之争使帝国分裂为四：中国的元朝、伊朗的伊儿汗国、中亚的察合台汗国和西部草原的金帐汗国。1368年元朝末代皇帝逃离大都，但此后数百年间，成吉思汗血统仍是草原上衡量统治合法性的标准。

summary.en: The Jochid khanate of the western steppe, ruled from Sarai on the lower Volga, held the Rus’ principalities as tributaries, converted to Islam under Özbeg, and broke up in the 15th century into the Kazan, Crimean, Astrakhan and other khanates.
summary.zh: 金帐汗国是术赤系在西部草原建立的汗国，以伏尔加河下游的萨莱为都，令罗斯诸公国称臣纳贡，在月即别汗时皈依伊斯兰教，15世纪分裂为喀山、克里米亚、阿斯特拉罕等汗国。

sources.title: Charles J. Halperin, Russia and the Golden Horde (1985)
Timothy May, The Mongol Conquests in World History (2012)
Wikidata Q79965

note: Capital coordinates are those of Selitrennoye, the site of Sarai Batu.

story.en:
The Golden Horde grew from the ulus that Genghis Khan gave his eldest son Jochi, the lands “as far west as Mongol hooves have trod”. Jochi’s son Batu, after the great western campaign of 1236–42, made his base on the lower Volga, where he founded Sarai. Its khans ruled the Cuman steppe from the Danube to Siberia, and collected tribute from the Rus’ principalities through patents (yarlyks) granted to obedient princes.

The khanate was a trading power as much as a nomad state. Sarai became a large city of craftsmen and merchants, Genoese and Venetians traded through Caffa and Tana in the Crimea, and an alliance with Mamluk Egypt sent steppe slaves south to become soldiers and sultans. Under Özbeg Khan (1313–41) the court adopted Islam.

Plague, the dynastic chaos of the “great troubles” after 1359 and the devastating campaign of Timur in 1395 broke its power. By the fifteenth century it had split into the khanates of Kazan, Crimea, Astrakhan and the Great Horde, whose last remnant was destroyed in 1502.
story.zh:
金帐汗国源于成吉思汗分给长子术赤的兀鲁思，即“蒙古马蹄所及的西方之地”。术赤之子拔都在1236—1242年的西征之后，以伏尔加河下游为根据地，建立萨莱城。其诸汗统治从多瑙河到西伯利亚的钦察草原，并通过颁给顺从王公的“札儿里黑”（敕书），向罗斯诸公国征收贡赋。

汗国既是游牧国家，也是商业强国。萨莱发展为工匠和商人聚居的大城；热那亚人和威尼斯人经克里米亚的卡法和塔纳进行贸易；与马木留克埃及的同盟则把草原奴隶输往南方，他们在那里成为士兵乃至苏丹。月即别汗（1313—1341年在位）时期，宫廷皈依伊斯兰教。

瘟疫、1359年后汗位更迭的“大混乱”以及1395年帖木儿的毁灭性征伐，摧毁了它的力量。十五世纪时它已分裂为喀山、克里米亚、阿斯特拉罕诸汗国和大帐汗国，后者的最后残余于1502年被消灭。

summary.en: Granted to Genghis Khan’s second son Chagatai, the khanate ruled Transoxiana and the Ili and Tarim regions; it split in the 1340s, with Timur’s emirs dominating the west and Moghulistan khans persisting in the east until the late 17th century.
summary.zh: 察合台汗国为成吉思汗次子察合台的封地，统治河中、伊犁和塔里木地区；14世纪40年代分裂，西部被帖木儿等埃米尔控制，东部的东察合台汗国（蒙兀儿斯坦）延续至17世纪末。

sources.title: Michal Biran, Qaidu and the Rise of the Independent Mongol State in Central Asia (1997)
Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
Wikidata Q487829

note: Wikidata spans 1225–1687 including Moghulistan; many works end the unified khanate in the 1340s. Tughlugh Timur ruled Moghulistan from 1347 and the whole khanate 1360–1363.

summary.en: Built by Timur’s conquests, the empire shrank under his successors but sponsored a brilliant Persianate culture of architecture, miniature painting, science and Chagatai poetry in Samarkand and Herat until the Uzbeks overran it.
summary.zh: 帖木儿帝国由帖木儿的征服建立，其后继者时期疆域收缩，但在撒马尔罕和赫拉特孕育了建筑、细密画、科学与察合台诗歌交相辉映的波斯化文化，直至被乌兹别克人征服。

sources.title: Beatrice Forbes Manz, The Rise and Rule of Tamerlane (1989)
Thomas W. Lentz & Glenn D. Lowry, Timur and the Princely Vision (1989)
Encyclopaedia Britannica: Timurid dynasty
Wikidata Q484195

story.en:
Timur’s conquests made Samarkand the capital of an empire stretching from Anatolia to the borders of India, but his heirs fought over it as soon as he died in 1405. His youngest surviving son Shah Rukh won, ruled from Herat, and left Samarkand to his own son Ulugh Beg.

The century that followed is remembered less for conquest than for culture. Shah Rukh’s wife Gawhar Shad built mosques and madrasas in Herat and Mashhad; Ulugh Beg built his observatory; and under the last great Timurid, Sultan Husayn Bayqara (1469–1506), Herat was the home of the poet Jami, the Turkic poet and minister Ali-Shir Nava’i and the painter Behzad. Persian miniature painting, calligraphy, the illuminated book and the tiled, double-domed architecture of the period shaped art from Istanbul to Delhi.

Politically the empire shrank to rival principalities. Muhammad Shaybani’s Uzbeks took Samarkand in 1500 and Herat in 1507. One Timurid prince, Babur, escaped to Kabul and founded the Mughal empire in India.
story.zh:
帖木儿的征服使撒马尔罕成为一个西起安纳托利亚、东至印度边境的帝国首都，但1405年他一去世，继承人们就争夺起来。他最小的在世儿子沙哈鲁最终胜出，以赫拉特为都，把撒马尔罕交给自己的儿子兀鲁伯。

此后一个世纪令人记住的与其说是征服，不如说是文化。沙哈鲁之妻高哈尔·沙德在赫拉特和马什哈德兴建清真寺与经学院；兀鲁伯修建天文台；在最后一位伟大的帖木儿君主速檀忽辛·拜哈拉（1469—1506年在位）时期，赫拉特聚集了诗人贾米、突厥语诗人兼大臣纳沃伊和画家贝赫扎德。这一时期的波斯细密画、书法、彩饰书籍以及贴满彩砖的双层穹顶建筑，影响了从伊斯坦布尔到德里的艺术。

政治上，帝国萎缩为相互敌对的诸侯国。昔班尼的乌兹别克人于1500年夺取撒马尔罕，1507年夺取赫拉特。帖木儿后裔巴布尔逃往喀布尔，后来在印度建立了莫卧儿帝国。

summary.en: Founded by Kerei and Janibek, the khanate united the Kazakh nomads, later divided into the Great, Middle and Little Hordes, fought long wars with the Dzungars, and was gradually absorbed by Russia, which abolished the last khans by the 1840s.
summary.zh: 哈萨克汗国由克烈与贾尼别克建立，统一了哈萨克游牧部落，后分为大、中、小三个玉兹，与准噶尔长期交战，逐渐被俄国吞并，至19世纪40年代末代可汗被废。

sources.title: Martha Brill Olcott, The Kazakhs, 2nd ed. (1995)
Mirza Muhammad Haidar Dughlat, Tarikh-i Rashidi
Wikidata Q1433867

note: Early khans’ reign dates are approximate. The end date 1847 (Wikidata) marks the death of Kenesary Khan.

summary.en: Established by Muhammad Shaybani’s Uzbeks on the ruins of the Timurid state, the khanate was ruled by Shaybanid and then Janid (Ashtarkhanid) khans, flourishing under Abdullah Khan II before declining into rule by Manghit atalyqs.
summary.zh: 布哈拉汗国由穆罕默德·昔班尼率领的乌兹别克人在帖木儿国家废墟上建立，先后由昔班尼王朝与札尼王朝（阿斯特拉罕王朝）统治，在阿卜杜拉汗二世时繁荣，后衰落并由曼吉特部的阿塔雷克掌权。

sources.title: R. D. McChesney, “Central Asia vi. In the 16th–18th centuries”, Encyclopaedia Iranica
History of Civilizations of Central Asia, vol. V (UNESCO)
Wikidata Q577668

summary.en: The Manghit dynasty took the title of emir in 1785; Bukhara became a Russian protectorate in 1868 after losing Samarkand, and the Red Army overthrew the last emir, Alim Khan, in 1920.
summary.zh: 曼吉特王朝于1785年改称埃米尔；1868年失去撒马尔罕后布哈拉成为俄国保护国，1920年红军推翻末代埃米尔阿利姆汗。

sources.title: Seymour Becker, Russia’s Protectorates in Central Asia: Bukhara and Khiva, 1865–1924 (1968)
Adeeb Khalid, Central Asia: A New History from the Imperial Conquests to the Present (2021)
Wikidata Q746558

summary.en: The last great nomadic empire, the Oirat Dzungar state dominated the Ili valley, Tarim basin and Kazakh steppe, contested Tibet and Khalkha with the Qing, and was annihilated by Qing armies in 1755–1758.
summary.zh: 准噶尔汗国是最后一个强大的游牧帝国，卫拉特准噶尔部称雄伊犁河谷、塔里木盆地和哈萨克草原，与清朝争夺西藏和喀尔喀，1755—1758年被清军彻底消灭。

name.zh: 阿睦尔撒纳（反清自立者）

sources.title: Peter C. Perdue, China Marches West: The Qing Conquest of Central Eurasia (2005)
Thomas J. Barfield, The Perilous Frontier: Nomadic Empires and China (1989)
